revisits.item: In a report crowded with marginal findings, the result that ought to have been the most ___ (that the drug's benefit vanished entirely in patients over sixty) was relegated to a footnote, as though its authors hoped no one would weigh how badly it undercut their conclusion. · choices: futile / conspicuous / spurious / nugatory / salient / estimable
revisits.change: new sentence logic: a contrast instead of a cause, or a concession instead of a restatement

revisits.item: By the time the chair finished her interminable opening remarks, the delegates had grown (i) ___, shifting in their seats and muttering to their neighbors. So when a junior delegate answered a pointed question with a joke about the chair's tie, the reply struck the room as (ii) ___ enough that two senior members walked out. He later insisted that he had meant only to lighten the mood, but even his allies conceded that, whatever its intent, the jest had been (iii) ___: the moment called for gravity, and he had offered a prank. · blank 1: crestfallen / restive / aloof; blank 2: untoward / fanciful / arduous; blank 3: puerile / philistine / artless
revisits.change: new format: an SE item becomes a TC blank, or a TC blank becomes an SE pair

revisits.item: Those who expected the older ensemble's players to soften once the merger raised their salaries had misjudged the source of the grievance. The players remained (i) ___, treating each conciliatory gesture from management as one more proof of the original slight. Far from forging a common identity, joint rehearsals seemed only to (ii) ___ new quarrels, and within three seasons the board conceded what the players had predicted from the start, voting for the (iii) ___ of the combined orchestra. · blank 1: pugnacious / compliant / implacable; blank 2: substantiate / engender / supersede; blank 3: schism / hegemony / dissolution
revisits.change: a different SE partner or a different sense of the word

revisits.item: That the settlement passed with so little dissent says less about its terms than about how few of the shareholders had (i) ___ them: anyone who read past the two-page summary would have found that the division of assets, (ii) ___ in the summary's telling, in fact left the founders with nearly all of the voting power. · blank 1: misconstrued / perused / supplanted; blank 2: ersatz / replete / equitable
revisits.change: a new context and no distractor shared with the earlier item
